title: Balkan Slavic Digital Editions (Pop Punčov Sbornik, Life of St. Petka, Tale of Alexander, Excerpts)
institution: University of Zurich, Institute of Slavic Studies (SNSF project 176378, Barbara Sonnenhauser) and Czech Academy of Sciences; hosted at LMU Munich (Ivan Šimko, Anastasia Escher)
notes: Corpus of Balkan Slavic texts from the 10th to the 19th century collected for the study of linguistic change: Pop Punčo's Sbornik (1796), the Life of St. Petka in many copies, the Tale of Alexander the Elder, and an Excerpts sub-corpus. Texts come with English translations, morphological and syntactic annotation, search and facsimiles. Sources within 1450-1700 include Vuković's Zbornik za putnike (printed 1536), the Joseph-Volokolamsk manuscript of 1537, the Tikhonravov damaskin and other 17th-century damaskini, Šimun Kozičić (1530s), and Letters of Wallachian princes. Texts are read in the web interface; no bulk download was found. Number of texts and words in 1450-1700 not given because the share cannot be established from the site; the whole corpus is much larger and mostly outside the period. Status active: the home page was modified in July 2026 and the Excerpts page in February 2026.
